data.name: Garrison
data.gender_notes: Garrison is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A stronghold or fortification, derived from the Old English words 'gars' (spear) and 'dun' (hill). In a metaphorical sense, it represents a person of great strength, courage, and determination. The name Garrison carries the meaning “Stronghold, fortification” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Garrison usually hope their child will grow to embody stronghold, fortification and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of protection and security in the spiritual realm.
data.etymology: Garrison belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Stronghold, fortification.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Garrison total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: עגירון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עגרון (עָגִירוֹן) - צבאי, גדוד, איש צבא. בעברית עתיקה, המילה עגירון מיוחסת לעגר, כלומר 'להכין' או 'להכניס'. כיום, השם עגירון נפוץ כשם משפחה, ובו נגזרה הצורה עגירון.

in_greek.name: Γαρίσων
in_greek.long_meaning: Γαρίσων (Γαρίσων) - στρατηγός, διοικητής, αξιωματικός. Η λέξη Γαρίσων προέρχεται από τα αρχαία ελληνικά και αναφέρεται σε ένα αξιωματικό ή διοικητή. Στη Βίβλο, ο Γαρίσων είναι ένα επώνυμο που αναφέρεται σε έναν στρατηγό από την Ταρσό (Κολόσσαι 4:11-12).

in_latin.name: Garrison
in_latin.long_meaning: Garrison - miles, armiger, miles Romanus. Latinus origo nominis a milite, armiger, miles Romanus. Nomen militare originem habet ab armigero, qui miles erat Romani exercitus.

in_english.name: Garrison
in_english.meaning: a military officer, a fortification, or a stronghold
in_english.long_meaning: Garrison - a military officer, a fortification, or a stronghold. The name Garrison has its origins in the Old French word 'garrison', which means a group of soldiers stationed in a fortified place. In the Christian tradition, the name Garrison is associated with strength, courage, and protection. It is also linked to the biblical figure of Garrison, a Roman officer who was converted to Christianity (Acts 6:5).

data.cultural_impact: In the context of Christianity, the name Garrison carries historical significance as it is associated with early Christian settlements or fortified congregations called Garrison Churches. These churches were often built in strategic locations, establishing a strong Christian presence in areas susceptible to enemy attacks.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Garrison can be derived from its biblical origins. In the book of Joshua (1:18), the phrase "a man of war who shall go out before them" refers to the set-apart individual – a "Garrison" – a faithful spiritual leader and protector, dedicated to upholding God’s commandments and ensuring the community remains steadfast in its faith.
